title: Languages & Greetings — A Multilingual Welcome
strapline: Hello, bonjour, salaam, namaste — every language is welcome here.
intent: Hearing and using greetings in many languages tells every child that their home language belongs and is valued here.
Playing with the sounds of different languages builds listening, phonological awareness and delight in words.
Learning to say hello, please and thank you in friends' languages grows respect, kindness and community.
Children with more than one language get to be the expert, sharing and teaching their words.
The theme opens curiosity about how people all over the world talk, sing and welcome each other.
implementation: Learn and use a rotating greeting each day or week — hello and goodbye in the languages of the children in the room.
Invite families to record or teach a greeting, a counting rhyme or a lullaby in their home language.
Wonder together at the sounds: 'What does hello sound like in Amara's language? Shall we all try it?'
Let children who speak another language lead — teaching a word, correcting our pronunciation, feeling proud.
Add multilingual labels, welcome signs and dual-language books so print in many languages is visible and normal.
Keep it warm and celebratory — every attempt is applauded, every language is a gift to the room.
key_questions: How do you say hello in your language — can you teach us?
What sounds different about this greeting?
How does your family say goodbye at bedtime?
Can you count to three in another language with me?
Which greeting shall we use to welcome everyone today?

impact.text: Children use greetings in more than one language and value the languages around them.
Children listen closely to and play with the sounds of different languages.
Children who speak another language share and teach their words with pride.
Children show kindness and welcome to friends from many backgrounds.
Children notice print and welcome in many languages around the room.

enhancements: A rotating 'greeting of the week' board with words from the room's home languages.
Family-recorded greetings, counting rhymes and lullabies to listen to.
Dual-language books and multilingual welcome signs and labels.
A hello-around-the-world song or circle-time routine.
A 'languages we speak' family display celebrating the room's languages.

playing_exploring: Children try out new sounds and greetings with delight.
They listen to and play with languages from around the room and world.
active_learning: Children practise a new greeting until they can say it confidently.
Children who know a language take pride in teaching it to others.
creating_thinking: Children notice how languages sound the same and different.
They connect words to friends, families and places.
